name: Leucine
lead: Leucine is an essential branched-chain amino acid found in all dietary proteins, with especially high amounts in dairy, meat, eggs and soy. It is also sold as a standalone powder or as part of BCAA and essential amino acid products.

In the muscle-building context it is used to push muscle protein synthesis, particularly in older adults or in people eating little protein. The strong rating reflects solid mechanistic and acute-response data, though extra isolated leucine adds little for people who already eat enough complete protein.

paras: Leucine acts as a signal of amino acid availability. Sensors such as Sestrin2 respond to intracellular leucine and release inhibition of the mTORC1 complex, which promotes translation initiation and muscle protein synthesis. Insulin release triggered by leucine contributes to the same pathway.

Leucine is a normal dietary component and legal. High supplemental doses can cause digestive upset and may disturb the balance of other branched-chain amino acids, and it is dangerous in maple syrup urine disease. Long-term muscle-growth benefits from isolated leucine in healthy, well-fed trainees are not well demonstrated.
